description.narrative: This project aims to improve livelihood and local economic recovery as critical drivers for peace and social cohesion in the conflict-affected communities in Darfur. It is an evidence-based project based on a tried and tested model, drawing on lessons learned from the previous phase. Social/economic infrastructure including warehouses, water yards, a community center, and livelihood hubs to support economic recovery and peaceful co-existence in 7 localities in North, South, and East Darfur states. The infrastructure includes a health facility, warehouses, potable water for humans and livestock, construction of livelihood hubs. Over 30,000 individuals, including nomads, IDPs, returnees, and host communities, are expected to benefit from these community assets. Women constitute about 53 percent of the beneficiaries.
Additionally, The Project supported the groundnut value chains in South and East Darfur states by providing farm machinery, improved agro-inputs, start-up capital, and improved new agricultural technologies through public-private partnerships (PPP) arrangements. The PPP has also created 1,500 jobs in Darfur by providing farm labor and factory jobs, with more than 90 percent youth. Also, through this partnership, the Project contributed to improving the nutritional status of over 2 million malnourished children in Darfur through the processing of groundnuts into Plumpy Nuts - nutrient-dense RUTF produced by DARFOOD in Edaen. The Project also partnered with DALFOOD to support the livestock value chain in Ed El Fursan to improve the livestock breeds in South Darfur to improve milk and beef production.

The Project contributed to these outcomes by directly supporting 2,220 households in conflict-affected communities to engage in livelihood and economic recovery activities, covering 9 localities in North Darfur, Central Darfur, and West Darfur. The Project established 31 Producer Associations and Voluntary Savings and Lending Associations in North Darfur, Central Darfur, and West Darfur, with a total membership of 1,960, with 52% women. The Project built the capacity of the associations and supported them to engage in economic activities. It also restored and replaced the productive assets of about 2,000 vulnerable households, especially the women-headed households, to enable them to re-engage in economic activities. A survey conducted revealed that 59% of the targeted households increased their assets. Disaggregating by gender, 63% and 54% of men and women increased their household assets. A survey revealed that 90% of the population believed that there had been a decrease in humanitarian needs and increased self-reliance.
The project rehabilitated the Gum Arabic center in Silea town, including the construction of a latrine and rehabilitation of the Gum Arabic nursery fitted with an irrigation facility to produce 10,000 seedlings. Cumulatively, the Project has constructed/rehabilitated 17 social/economic infrastructure, including warehouses, water yards, a community center, and livelihood hubs to support economic recovery and peaceful co-existence in 9 localities in the North, South, Central, and East Darfur states. Over 40,000 individuals, including nomads, IDPs, returnees, and host communities, are expected to benefit from these community assets. Women constitute about 53% of the beneficiaries. About 50 vulnerable women and youth (53% female) were employed in a temporary labor-intensive scheme to construct the above infrastructure during the period. Overall, 80% of the population (male 73%; female 88%) in the project intervention area have access to critical basic services and productive community assets. Overall, there has been an improvement in access to critical infrastructure by 51%.
In 2022, the Project established four (4) additional Peace and Development Committees (PDCs) to support peacebuilding and socio-economic recovery in the conflict-affected communities in North Darfur, bringing the total PDCs established to 37. The PDCs members were trained in mediation and negotiation skills, data collection, incidence monitoring, and reporting skills and were equipped with stationeries and record books. Over 37,000 community members are benefiting from the activities of the PDCs. A survey conducted indicated that 100% of the community members have access to community conflict resolution mechanisms established by the project. 88% indicated a decrease in natural resource-related conflicts. disaggregating by gender, 86% of the men reported a reduction in natural resource-related disputes, while 89% of the women reported the same. This includes a reduction in conflicts over land due to the intervention of the PDCs, a reduction in the competition over water resources, and easy access to land among returnees and vulnerable groups facilitated by the project and the PDCs. Averagely, 20 natural resource-related conflicts were reported in the project intervention states, with West Darfur recording above the average of 25 and East Darfur recording the least (3 cases). Women reported 43 cases, while men reported 16 cases. 90% of all the cases were resolved. However, 65% of the cases reported by women were resolved, while 100% of the cases reported by men were resolved. The project is paying greater attention to increasing productivity through improved cultural practices and intensification rather than the increasing area under production. According to FAO (2020), the national average yield of groundnuts under rainfed is 0.85 per hectare. Compared with the performance of the L4P interventions, the project has made positive strides toward enhancing productivity. Productivity in 2019 was 0.9 MT per hectare and 0.81 MT per hectare in 2020. In 2021, the project registered a signification increase in productivity to about 1.47 metric tons per hectare.
The Project continued to engage with the Government counterparts at the grassroots level, building their capacity to support the economic recovery of the conflict-affected communities. In 2021, the project conducted institutional capacity assessments in Government institutions working on durable solutions and economic recovery. The institutions were the Voluntary Return and Resettlement Commission, Microfinance institutions, Greater Darfur Microfinance Apex, and the Ministry of Finance. The outcome of the assessment was the design of a training program to build the capacity of government employees. 5 key training workshops have been planned on ICT, leadership, community mobilization, arbitration, planning, monitoring, and evaluation across the five (5) states of Darfur. 20 staff from the Ministry of Animal Production were trained on artificial insemination techniques. Capacity-building activities have been completed. Six field days were organized in collaboration with the Government counterparts.
